mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp deceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1.5% month-over-month, coinciding with rising raw material prices (RSAFS), signals input-cost inflation and supply chain stress, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO MoM change < -1.5% AND RSAFS MoM change > 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO decelerates by >1.5% MoM and RSAFS rises by >2% MoM simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 1% signals an emergency easing in response to financial stress, which boosts risk appetite and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 1% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls below 1% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month indicates labor market churning, which can precede earnings downgrades and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE and PAYEMS rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during three consecutive months where HOUST is above its 12-month moving average by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent divergence between real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth—where GDPC1 grows slower than PAYEMS for four consecutive quarters—signals underutilized labor and weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < PAYEMS growth for 4 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 growth lags PAYEMS growth for four consecutive quarters.
